requirements.value: Two CW tones (f1, f2) of equal specified power combined and fed to the device; the tones' own harmonics/self-IM must sit at least 10 dB below the IM level expected from the device
requirements.note: Summarized in our words; buy the standard for the exact text.

requirements.value: 2 x 20 W (2 x 43 dBm) at the device's test port is the general recommendation for mobile communication systems unless the test spec says otherwise; other systems may need higher or lower power; never exceed the device's power rating
requirements.note: The power-handling limit was added in the 2025 edition. Anritsu notes many operators also adopted 2 x 20 W for site testing because no field power standard existed.

requirements.item: Residual (self) IM of the test set-up
requirements.value: Set-up self-IM, including the load, should be at least 10 dB below the level being measured
requirements.note: Anritsu's reading of the IEC error curve: 10 dB margin gives up to +2/-3 dB error, 5 dB gives +4/-7 dB, 20 dB gives under 1 dB.

requirements.value: Products such as (2f1 - f2) and (2f2 - f1); 3rd order is usually the worst case and is normally sufficient, but the set-ups can measure other orders
PIM is typically frequency dependent and must be investigated over the specified band; swept or multiple fixed frequencies often give more accurate results
requirements.note: New emphasis in Ed. 3.0 (2025).

requirements.value: Reverse (reflected) set-up suits one-port and multi-port devices; forward (transmitted) suits two/multi-port only; multi-port analyzers are an allowed topology
requirements.note: Field analyzers (Anritsu, Kaelus, Rosenberger, AWT) measure reverse PIM.

requirements.value: On multi-port devices, terminate unused ports in a linear (low-IM) termination rated for the power
Check power handling, frequency range, cleanliness and interface dimensions; tighten every connector interface to the IEC interface spec or, if none, to the manufacturer's value

requirements.item: What a test specification must state
requirements.value: Test power; IM order; forward or reverse; band(s) or exact frequencies; dynamic stimulus while testing; maximum allowable PIM
requirements.note: IEC itself sets no pass/fail level; the owner's spec does.

requirements.value: State input power per tone, f1 and f2, the PIM level and its frequency; report the maximum PIM over the test duration
Measurement only; the series does not address long-term reliability of a product
requirements.note: Anritsu (2017) noted the then-current edition addressed factory testing only; field testing arrived with Part 7 in 2022.

requirements.value: Reverse PIM measurement of deployed systems, either terminated into low-PIM loads or through antennas that radiate the tones
Stay within government limits on authorized RF radiation; keep keys, phones, ladders and tools out from in front of / near the antenna

f1 and f2 must pass through the whole system and the IM product must return to the analyzer; bypass blocking devices with short low-PIM jumpers; place f1/f2 in guard bands; survey local spectrum first and move the IM product to unused spectrum if interference is seen
Stay a safe distance from radiating antennas; lock off every radio feeding the line under test before disconnecting at the radio port (RF burn risk)
Must perform reverse PIM per IEC 62037-1 set-up 1 and be ruggedized for shock, vibration and uncontrolled temperature
Unless specified otherwise, inject the tones at the connector where the radio's transmit signal enters the system
Clean every set-up connector with isopropyl alcohol and a lint-free wipe; remove all metal flakes; replace worn or damaged parts
Test lead + adapters into a low-PIM termination, flexing the lead; peak self-IM at least 10 dB below the level to be measured
A known PIM standard (with termination) on the analyzer port must read within 3 dB of its stated value
Below 1.92:1 (10 dB return loss) at f1, f2 and the IM frequency, unless specified otherwise; fix high reflections before PIM testing
With the tones off, external signal at the IM frequency should be at least 10 dB below the IM level to be measured
Run static first; if above the limit, repair before dynamic. Fixed frequencies can falsely pass when two sources cancel (180 deg); swept tests guard against that
Peak IM during the dynamic stimulus must not exceed the pass/fail level; use fixed frequencies for responsiveness; field stimulus must not be harsher than the relevant component part of IEC 62037
Hold at 4 x the specified repeated bend radius; rotate 3 cycles; rotation radius about cable diameter + 10 mm
5 impacts per connector with a non-damaging tool (plastic screwdriver end, rubberized wrench end); energy no more than IEC 62037-3 Table 1 for that connector; never strike the cable
requirements.note: The Table 1 energies are in the paywalled IEC 62037-3 and were not available.

requirements.item: Dynamic stimulus: splitters, combiners, filters, LNAs
requirements.value: 2 impacts on the body next to each connector; 3 impacts along each side with no connector; at most 0.14 J per impact
Strike the rear surface: 2 impacts next to each connector, then every 30 cm along the height; at most 1 J per impact; avoid radome and fragile parts
Residual PIM of the measurement system and the peak PIM of each feed line under dynamic loading
Procedure for jumpers and assemblies that move in service; 2021 edition ties mechanical stress to the advertised bend radius
Impact test to check connectors' resistance to weak contacts and loose particles, separating connector PIM from cable PIM
Fixtures and procedures for cable PIM: two dynamic methods and one static method
Qualification and acceptance methods for low-IM filters; 2021 edition defines impact energy and impact locations
Fixtures/procedures for antenna PIM qualification and acceptance; 2021 edition defines impact energy and locations; Amendment 1 (2025) makes reported values the maximum PIM
requirements.note: Bibliography points to IEC 60068-2-75 hammer tests.

requirements.value: Radiated test of PIM from any object or material exposed to RF (near or far field; outdoor site or anechoic chamber)
requirements.note: Useful background for external 'rusty bolt' PIM.

requirements.value: The 2018 IFC Section 510 text contains no PIM, sweep, return-loss or VSWR requirement
requirements.note: Checked the full reproduced text. Section numbers shift in IFC 2021/2024 (e.g., acceptance test moves); verify the edition your AHJ adopted.

requirements.value: Isolation between donor and all inside antennas at least 20 dB greater than system gain under all operating conditions
requirements.note: Not a PIM test, but measured on the same visit.

requirements.value: The fire code official keeps a document listing required frequencies, radio sites, ERP, max propagation delay, applications
requirements.note: Use this frequency list to compute which IM products can land in ERCES uplinks.

requirements.value: Two-way coverage not less than 95% per floor; 20 equal grid areas; calibrated portable radio of the agency's model
Install/test/maintain ERCES: acceptance, annual and five-yearly quantitative re-test; DAQ 3.0 in 95% of general and 99% of critical areas
requirements.note: NFPA text not opened (paywalled); the SBC primer that summarizes it does not mention PIM. No source found that makes PIM testing a code requirement.

requirements.value: Pre-acceptance documentation includes antenna and cable sweep results and 'PIM Testing results (if applicable)'
requirements.note: Example of an AHJ asking for PIM results without setting a limit.

requirements.value: Technicians are expected to define PIM, describe a PIM tester, and interpret antenna line sweeps (RL, IL, DTF)
requirements.note: Training scope, not a code requirement.

requirements.value: Sweep every cable segment around 160, 460, 700, 840, 930 and 1925 MHz; return loss over 20 dB at any connector; inspect and clean all connectors before mating; prefer factory-made passive assemblies to reduce PIM
requirements.note: No numeric PIM limit in this spec. Its blanket torque line (16-18 ft-lb or manufacturer) fits 7/16 DIN only - see torque table.

requirements.value: AT&T's MOP sets PIM pass/fail values; not public. Anritsu describes the flow: 1-port PIM vs time + swept PIM, DTP if failing, 2-port test (F1 on band 14 antenna, F2 on band 17 antenna) for external IM3, LTE-M Pilot as the network-side check
requirements.note: Values come only via the carrier/contract. Secondary source only.

requirements.value: No public PIM acceptance spec found
requirements.note: Anritsu: acceptable PIM is set by the site/equipment owner and must be specified at procurement with test parameters and power. Get the MOP from the carrier or GC.

requirements.value: 'Most operators' require IM3 at -140 dBc with 2 x 20 W tones (DAS context)
requirements.note: Vendor statement, not a carrier document.

requirements.value: Each passive DAS segment at the multi-network combiner <= -140 dBc at design power; segments <= 5 W: <= -140 dBc with 2 x 33 dBm; test low/mid/high bands; PIM vs time >= 10 s; calibrated analyzer; hand over original result files
requirements.note: Public carrier-forum spec from Australia; useful model, not binding in the US.

requirements.value: Splitters/couplers <= -150 dBc @ 2 x 43 dBm; terminations <5 W <= -140 dBc @ 2 x 33 dBm; terminations >=5 W <= -150 dBc @ 2 x 43 dBm; patch cables <= -150 dBc @ 2 x 43 dBm static and dynamic; no braided/foil cables (e.g., LMR400, RG214); no joiners or inter-series adapters

requirements.item: IWPC PIM Testing Best Practices (TTER, Nov 2014)
requirements.value: Field best-practice document cited by the MCF spec; quoted as saying lower test power may be required for small cell and DAS testing
requirements.note: Not opened: download requires an IWPC request form. Content known only via MCF and Valmont citations.

items.detail: Limit, test power, IM order, bands or exact F1/F2, dynamic stimulus, test duration. IEC lists these as what a test spec must state.
Carrier MOP, neutral host, or building owner. Limits are set by the site/equipment owner; carrier MOPs (e.g., AT&T) are not public.

items.step: Pick analyzer band(s) that pass the system
items.detail: Each analyzer is band-specific. Check filter combiners/diplexers in the path: F1, F2 and the IM product must all pass, or plan to bypass that device.

items.step: Plan F1/F2 and check the IM product frequency
items.detail: Put F1/F2 in guard bands and land the IM product in unused spectrum; survey local signals first.
Testing into an antenna outside a chamber may breach licensing; get advance permission from licensees who could be affected.
The path must be off-air. CommScope/Andrew prefer evening maintenance windows and testing lines into loads to limit radiation.
Analyzer can put out up to 2 x 40 W (80 W). Confirm DAS antennas, dividers and loads can take the planned test power.
As-built drawing, cable types and velocity factor, prior DTF-RL-Load and DTF-RL-Short traces for DTP/DTF overlay.
Analyzer calibration current; carriers' DAS specs require a validly calibrated instrument.

Low-PIM termination(s), PIM standard, low-PIM test cable and adapters (not line-sweep precision adapters), torque wrenches for each connector type, cleaning wipes and swabs, steel wool in a plastic bag plus painter's tape (PIM marker).

items.step: ERCES jobs: get the AHJ frequency list
items.detail: The fire code official's technical criteria document lists the required frequencies; use it to compute which IM products can hit the uplinks.

checklists.name: On-site safety
checklists.when: On arrival, before any connector is opened

items.detail: Lock off and confirm non-transmitting every radio feeding the line before disconnecting at the radio port (RF burn risk).
When testing through antennas, stay a safe distance away and do not stand in front of or under the antenna; nobody touches antennas under test.
Move keys, phones, ladders and tools away from the front of the antenna; tower crew climbs away during the test (tools and safety belts create PIM).
Up to 80 W total is available; check every device in the path is rated for the test power.
Kaelus iXA/iPA shut down on high return loss; Anritsu files flag tests run with the High Reflection Warning bypassed. Investigate rather than bypass.
Follow EME precautions when testing a DAS with antennas connected.

checklists.name: Test setup and verification
checklists.when: Each time the analyzer is set up, and whenever results look wrong

items.detail: Anritsu MW82119B specs apply after 10 minutes powered on.
Analyzer port, test lead, adapters and load: isopropyl alcohol on a lint-free wipe, remove metal flakes, replace worn parts.
Calibration components and precision line-sweep adapters are not low-PIM and not rated for PIM power.
Seals on repeatedly mated test cables collect metal shavings that contaminate every later connection.
Test lead + adapters into a low-PIM load, flex the lead; peak must be at least 10 dB below the limit.
Standard + termination on the analyzer port reads within 3 dB of its stated value (Anritsu standard: -80 dBm +/-3 dB at 1730 MHz with 2 x 20 W).
Through the test lead and adapters at f1, f2 and the IM frequency: below 1.92:1 (10 dB RL) unless specified.
Tones off, receiver on: external signal at the IM frequency at least 10 dB below the limit; otherwise move F1/F2.
Power, F1, F2, IM order, duration and the pass/fail limit line in the instrument.
Carrier DAS specs ask for screenshots with correct local date and time.
Fixed F1/F2; run at least the spec duration (MCF: >= 10 s; AWT: >= 30 s to energize and heat the system). Readings should be stable; AWT treats 2-4 dB swings as acceptable.
Hold one tone, sweep the other across the receive band so phase cancellation between two sources cannot hide a failure.
Fixed frequencies, PIM vs time long enough to reach every point (Anritsu: 30-60 s typical). Tap/flex every connection; the peak must stay under the limit.
Report the maximum PIM over the test duration.

items.step: If it fails: DTP before touching anything
items.detail: Run Distance-to-PIM to see where the source is before opening good connections.
Save each measurement into a per-site directory; name/subtitle by sector and line for reporting.

checklists.name: Fault finding
checklists.when: After a failed static or dynamic test

items.detail: DTP shows PIM vs distance; overlay a DTF trace to map it to the nearest connector. Use the same velocity factor for both.
Tape steel wool (bagged) to the radome centre, store the DTP trace as a PIM marker, remove it at least 3 m, re-measure. Relative distance > 0: beyond antenna; = 0: at antenna; < 0: in feed/antenna.

items.step: Step through with a low-PIM load
items.detail: Move the low-PIM load along the line (or terminate divider outputs) to isolate the failing segment, then add branches back one at a time.

items.step: Work the connector at the hit
items.detail: Inspect, clean, re-torque or re-terminate; remove foam/adhesive that blocks metal-to-metal contact.
If one connector was installed wrong, most others by the same installer likely need attention.
Noise-floor imbalance between Rx diversity paths points to PIM in the noisy path; raised noise on both paths points outside the antenna system; site better after rain points to rusty mounts nearby.
Hunt beyond the antenna (PIM Hunter probe on the DTP distance arc); for cross-band IM3 between separate antennas use a 2-port test.
Moving a DAS antenna within about a 1 m circle away from the external source clears most external PIM without hurting coverage.
Repeat residual, static and dynamic after the repair; document any IM sources beyond the antenna for the owner.

checklists.name: Connector inspect, clean and torque
checklists.when: Every time a connector is opened or made

items.detail: Leave protective caps on until the mating cable is ready.
With a magnifier: no loose centre conductor, dents, scratches, metal flakes or corrosion; check centre-pin depth.
Low-pressure compressed air; a toothpick for particles the air leaves.
Isopropyl alcohol on a swab or lint-free wipe; use little, it can soften plastic parts.
Low-pressure air again to remove residue and dry.
Sharp, correct tools; cut with the cable facing down; deburr; keep foam and adhesive off contact surfaces; clean solder flux.
Align before mating; twisting scratches the centre pin.
Manufacturer value for that interface (see torque table); never over-torque.
Antenna connectors can loosen after a few torque cycles; troubleshoot DIN joints without the seal at hand-tight, then refit seals and torque for final certification.
Residual of the measurement system as tested.

items.step: Peak PIM per line under dynamic loading
items.detail: Plus static and swept results; dBm and dBc with test power.
F1, F2, power per tone, IM order, IM frequency, duration, limit, pass/fail.
Screenshots with date/time; original instrument files; DTP/DTF traces; photos.
Refit DIN seals removed during troubleshooting and torque; replace caps; reconnect radios and remove lock-off.
Table of all measurements and pass/fail (PDF or Excel).

checklists.name: DAS PIM
checklists.when: Whenever a DAS is built, expanded or troubleshot

items.detail: Sweep and PIM at cable, branch, floor, sector, then system level; high DAS loss hides defects if you only test at the head-end.
Low-power PIM test at each design location with a temporary antenna; if high, move about 1 m.
At least one low band (700-900 MHz) and one high band; MCF requires low, mid and high (3500 MHz where used).
Indoor DAS runs from 20 W down to 0.1 W; set PIM power close to what that point really sees.
Valmont: moving the test point in by L dB of loss relaxes the dBm limit by L and the dBc limit by 2L when power is also cut by L.
Each multi-network combiner input with outputs on a precision load; then each segment alone with the others terminated.
Sweep and PIM the riser with low-PIM terminations on the tapper outputs.
Filter combiners/diplexers that stop F1, F2 or the IM product: bypass with short low-PIM jumpers.
Treat each remote's RF port as the combiner point and PIM the passive network from there; never feed PIM tones into BDA/remote ports.
Keep antennas off cable trays, vents, AC units, flashing; no loose metal within 500 mm.
Carrier approved-material lists; solid-outer-conductor cable; no braided cables, joiners or inter-series adapters.
Codes (IFC 510, NFPA 1225) do not require PIM testing, but AHJs may ask for PIM results (e.g., DC OUC).

sops.name: Residual PIM check (set-up verification)
sops.purpose: Prove the analyzer, test lead and adapters are quiet enough before trusting any reading.

steps.detail: Power on and leave on for 10 minutes (Anritsu MW82119B spec condition).
Analyzer port, test cable, adapters, low-PIM load: IPA on lint-free wipe; remove metal flakes; replace worn parts.

steps.action: Assemble exactly as you will test
steps.detail: Test lead + every adapter you will use, terminated in a low-PIM termination. Torque each joint.
Same power, F1/F2 and IM order as the job's test spec.

steps.action: Run PIM vs time and flex the lead
steps.detail: Flex the test cable along its length during the run.
steps.acceptance: Peak residual at least 10 dB below the job limit (e.g., limit -150 dBc / -107 dBm at 2 x 43 dBm -> residual <= -117 dBm / -160 dBc)

steps.detail: Connect the PIM standard (with termination if in-line) directly on the analyzer port; measure IM3 at its stated frequencies and power.
steps.acceptance: Within 3 dB of the stated value (Anritsu 1091-446-R: -80 dBm +/-3 dB at 1730 MHz, 2 x 20 W)

steps.detail: Re-clean, swap test lead/adapters, re-torque; if it still fails, the instrument needs service.
Save the residual trace; it goes in the report.

sops.name: Static PIM test
sops.purpose: Measure the line's PIM at rest, fixed and swept.

steps.detail: Lock off radios feeding the line; disconnect at the radio port; inject at that connector.
Measure through the test lead at f1, f2 and the IM frequency.
Tones off, receiver on at the IM frequency.
steps.acceptance: External signal >= 10 dB below the limit

steps.detail: Spec power (2 x 43 dBm unless the spec says otherwise), F1/F2 in guard bands, IM3 (or spec order).
Fixed tones for the spec duration (MCF >= 10 s; AWT >= 30 s).
steps.acceptance: Peak below the limit; stable (AWT: 2-4 dB swing acceptable)

steps.detail: One tone fixed, the other swept so the IM product covers the receive band.
steps.acceptance: Peak below the limit across the sweep

steps.detail: Peak in dBm and dBc, F1, F2, power, IM order, IM frequency; save file named for site/sector/line.
Pass -> dynamic test. Fail -> fault finding (DTP) before dynamic.

sops.name: Dynamic tap test
sops.purpose: Find loose or unstable joints that only show under movement.

steps.action: Start PIM vs time at fixed frequencies
steps.detail: Long enough to reach every joint (Anritsu: 30-60 s typical; MW82119B allows 1-1200 s).
5 impacts each with the plastic end of a screwdriver or rubberized end of a wrench; never strike the coax; no harder than knocking on a door. IEC caps energy at the IEC 62037-3 Table 1 value.
Splitters, couplers, combiners, filters, LNAs: 2 impacts on the body by each connector; 3 along each connector-free side; <= 0.14 J.
Rear surface: 2 by each connector, then every 30 cm of height; <= 1 J; avoid fragile parts.

IEC: hold at 4 x repeated bend radius, rotate 3 cycles at radius ~ cable diameter + 10 mm. Anritsu: hold 12 in from the connector, move no more than 1 in off axis. AWT: ~10 cm circle, 10 turns each way.
Note which joint produced the spike; re-open, clean with alcohol, dry, re-torque, re-tap.
Peak PIM per line under dynamic loading.

sops.name: Distance-to-PIM fault location
sops.purpose: Find where a PIM source sits: in the feed, at the antenna, or beyond it.

steps.detail: Set correct cable velocity factor; DTP sweeps F1 or F2 to produce IM vs distance.
Manual: high-res DTF from a Site Master or Option 331 (100s of MHz). Automatic: low-res DTF through the PIM port. Resolution (m) = 150 x Vp / sweep width (MHz).
steps.acceptance: PIM peak lines up with a connector or device

steps.action: Make a PIM marker if the hit is near the antenna
steps.detail: Bagged steel wool taped to the radome centre; store trace as overlay.
Move it at least 3 m away; read relative distance between peaks; set Vp = 1.0 for distances in air.
steps.acceptance: > 0 beyond antenna; = 0 at antenna; < 0 inside feed/antenna

steps.detail: Inspect, clean, re-terminate, replace the component at the DTP location.
Walk the DTP distance arc with a PIM probe; for cross-band IM3 from separate antennas use 2-port mode (F1 port 1, F2 port 2).
Repeat static and dynamic; record mitigated sources and any left beyond the antenna for the owner.

sops.name: Connector inspection and cleaning
sops.purpose: Remove the most common cause of PIM: dirty, damaged or badly made connections.

steps.detail: Leave protective caps on until mating.
Magnifier: centre conductor tight, no dents/scratches, no metal flakes, no corrosion, correct pin depth.
Low-pressure compressed air; toothpick for stubborn particles.
Isopropyl alcohol on swab or lint-free wipe; minimum amount.
steps.acceptance: Mating surfaces free of oil, dirt, flux

steps.detail: Low-pressure air (moisture-free).
Align first; do not twist; hand-start the nut.
Calibrated torque wrench, manufacturer value (see torque table); hold the body with a second wrench where needed.
steps.acceptance: Clicks at the set value; no over-torque

sops.name: DAS passive network PIM test
sops.purpose: Verify a passive DAS (or the passive side of an active/hybrid DAS) from antennas to head-end.

steps.detail: Use power close to what the point sees in service (20 W down to 0.1 W indoors). MCF: <= 5 W segments at 2 x 33 dBm; larger segments at design power.
Start from the head-end limit (e.g., -97 dBm / -140 dBc at 2 x 43 dBm) and adjust for loss to that point (Valmont rule: dBm limit moves by 1 x loss, dBc by 2 x loss).
Before mounting, low-power PIM test at each design location; move ~1 m if high.
Sweep and PIM each cable, then each floor (antennas + cables + splitters).
Sweep and PIM the riser with low-PIM terminations on tapper outputs.
Each multi-network combiner input with outputs on a precision load; then each segment individually with the others terminated. Bypass filter combiners that block test tones.
From the DAS input with floors connected; low and high band (MCF: low, mid, high).
Terminate all divider outputs, re-add branches one at a time, then DTP/DTF on the failing branch.
Table of all results with pass/fail, date/time screenshots, original files.

torque.note: PIM is designed to be independent of torque; Rosenberger's comparison table writes '> 5 Nm'.
Has a release inhibitor against accidental loosening.
Same universal jack mates all three plug types.

torque.torque: Sources differ: > 25 N-m (Rosenberger); 25-30 N-m / 221-265 in-lb (Microwaves101 table); 20 ft-lb (~27 N-m) 'accepted' (Anritsu)
torque.tool: 1-1/4 in torque wrench listed in Anritsu's PIM kit (01-513-R); that it is the 7/16 wrench is inferred

das.detail: DAS can have thousands of RF joints. Insertion loss between a PIM source and the head-end cuts the PIM seen at the BTS by about 3.5 dB per dB of loss (2.5 dB/dB slope + 1 dB return path), so sources deep in the network matter less - but bad workmanship near indoor antennas has produced harmful PIM hundreds of metres from the input.
Indoor DAS power ranges from 20 W down to 0.1 W; test near the real power at each point. Low-power defects with slopes near 2.2 dB/dB can be worse in service than 20 W results suggest.

Derive internal limits from the head-end limit and the loss to that point: the dBm limit relaxes by 1 x loss and the dBc limit by 2 x loss when test power is reduced by the same loss (Valmont example: -87 dBm at +33 dBm through 10 dB = -97 dBm at the input). Applying the head-end number everywhere over-tests.

Antenna locations (pre-install), each cable, each floor, the riser (tapper outputs terminated), each sector, the full system from the DAS input; MCF adds each multi-network-combiner input and each segment individually.
Terminate all outputs of the floor's divider in low-PIM loads to prove the feed and divider, then add branches one at a time; DTP/DTF on the failing branch.
One low band (700-900 MHz) plus one high band is generally enough to find DAS PIM; MCF requires low, mid and high (3500 MHz where present) and accepts 2600 MHz in lieu of 3500 MHz under conditions.

Test tones and IM product must pass every device in the path; bypass filter combiners that block them. For hybrid DAS the remote unit is treated as the combiner point, and the passive network is PIM-tested from there. Check antennas and dividers are rated for the test power.

High-power terminations on hybrid combiners often have poor IM3. Where only one operator's main/diversity are combined, IM7/IM9 may be what lands in-band, so a 'poor IM3' load can be fine; where multiple operators/bands share the hybrid, use a low-PIM cable load.
Multiband, multicarrier signals mix at each passive stage, so components close to the sources need the best PIM ratings (CommScope 2014: -140 -> -150 dBc, moving to -153/-160 dBc).

Splitters/couplers/hybrids/duplexers -153 dBc (Rosenberger RSS); 4.3-10 splitters/couplers -161 dBc (Rosenberger); hybrid < -155 dBc at 2 x 43 dBm (Microlab); 138-960 MHz public-safety coupler <= -153 dBc (Norsat DDC240); in-building antenna -153 dBc at 2 x 20 W incl. 350-470 MHz (CommScope CMAX-D-TCPUSEi53).

Use solid-outer-conductor cable; braided/foil cables such as LMR400 and RG214 have poor PIM regardless of connectors. Plenum example: RFS ICA12-50JPL 1/2 in corrugated, NFPA 262/CMP/CATVP, solid inner and outer conductor (no dBc figure published on the page).

MCF allows 7-16, 4.3-10 and N (subject to lead carrier); no joiners or inter-series adapters in patch cables. Prefer factory-terminated, PIM-certified jumpers and compression connectors from the approved list.

Sweep from each end on runs over 400 ft, or measure insertion loss with a source at one end and a spectrum analyzer at the other. No published dBc PIM figure found for radiating cable or its connectors.

Small low-gain DAS antennas light up nearby metal (often behind the antenna): cable trays, vent pipes, AC ducts, flashing, loose metal. Keep 500 mm clear; avoid concealing antennas in ceiling cavities or low-profile antennas without a backplane - MCF says the lead carrier will not commission a DAS whose concealed antennas fail PIM.
Mount components to a solid surface with strain relief and tool access; components hung from plasterboard anchors pulled out and PIM became erratic.

Main DAS PIM causes: poor components, poor workmanship (installers not trained in carrier-grade RF), antenna placement, reflective objects near antennas. A real case: foam and glue in connectors near two antennas found by DTP/DTF 108-147 m down a branch.
PIM rises with power and traffic, so problems often appear once the DAS carries load; carriers stress-test to emulate full-power operation.

IFC 510 (2018 text) and the NFPA 1225 summaries contain no PIM requirement. AHJs may still ask for PIM results (DC OUC: 'PIM Testing results (if applicable)'). ETA's DAST certification expects technicians to know PIM testers.

Public-safety DAS must carry VHF and UHF (incl. 380, 700, 800 MHz) - low-PIM DAS antennas have been measured at 380/700/1920 MHz. Field PIM analyzers found: AWT UHF/TETRA (380-470 MHz) and the 700 MHz units; no VHF field analyzer found.

When public-safety 800 MHz downlinks (851-854 MHz NPSPAC) share passive hardware with cellular, compute IM products against every uplink: e.g., 2 x 853.0 - 869.5 = 836.5 MHz falls in the 824-849 MHz cellular uplink (computed example).

Sweep (RL/DTF) the DAS in small sections - high insertion loss masks reflections at the far end - then PIM test. Example plan: sweep 400-2700 MHz and PIM at 700 and 1900 MHz for public safety through LTE 2600.
Calibrated analyzer, PIM vs time >= 10 s, table of all results with pass/fail, date/time-stamped screenshots, original result files.

report_fields.why: Identifies the test record; Anritsu LST report headers and CommScope reports carry site-specific information.

report_fields.field: Sector / line / branch / DAS segment description
report_fields.why: Each feed line gets its own result; IEC 62037-7 reports peak PIM per feed line.
Field tests inject where the radio's transmit enters; DAS limits depend on where you test.
Analyzers are band-specific; results must say which band was tested.
Required in IEC reporting; results at different frequencies go in separate tables.
dBc is meaningless without the test power; IEC requires the input power.
Part of the test specification and the reported result.

report_fields.field: Test type: static, swept, dynamic; 1-port or 2-port
report_fields.why: Different tests catch different faults; dynamic peak is the IEC field report item.
MCF requires PIM vs time of at least 10 s; IEC 2025 reports the max over the duration.

report_fields.field: Result: peak PIM in dBm and dBc
report_fields.why: Anritsu reports can be set to dBm or dBc; record both to avoid confusion.
Report compares peak to the limit; the limit belongs to the owner/carrier.
Tabular pass/fail summary is a standard deliverable.
IEC 62037-7 report item; proves the reading is not the test gear.
Shows the analyzer read a known source correctly (within 3 dB).

report_fields.field: VSWR / return loss at test frequencies
report_fields.why: PIM test validity check (< 1.92:1) and separate sweep deliverable.
Shows where any PIM source sits; DTF-RL-Load and DTF-RL-Short are the typical companion traces.

report_fields.field: External PIM found beyond the antenna
report_fields.why: Often the operator's, not the installer's, responsibility; document with DTP data.
Required on screenshots; instrument clock set to local time.
CommScope reports include operator information.

report_fields.field: Analyzer make, model, serial, calibration date
report_fields.why: Carrier DAS specs require a validly calibrated instrument; Anritsu reports split results by instrument.
Hand over the raw result files, not just a PDF.
Screenshots/photographs of measurements are a stated deliverable; photos of repaired joints support the record.
Anritsu places such results in separate tables - flag it.

glossary.meaning: Unwanted signals made when two or more strong signals pass through a non-linear junction in 'passive' parts - connectors, cables, antennas, nearby rusty metal. Also called the diode effect or rusty bolt effect.
The two test tones (or carriers) whose mixing makes the IM products.
n + m in nF1 - mF2. IM3 = 2F1 - F2 and 2F2 - F1; IM5 = 3F1 - 2F2 and 3F2 - 2F1; IM7 = 4F1 - 3F2 and 4F2 - 3F1. Lower orders are usually stronger.
Products from modulated carriers are wider than the carriers: IM3 about 3x, IM5 about 5x the carrier bandwidth.
Absolute power relative to 1 mW (43 dBm = 20 W, 46 dBm = 40 W, 33 dBm = 2 W).
PIM level relative to one test tone: dBc = PIM dBm - tone dBm. At 2 x 43 dBm, -150 dBc = -107 dBm, -153 dBc = -110 dBm.
Two tones of 20 W each - the IEC 62037-1 general recommendation for mobile systems.
dB of PIM change per dB of tone power change. Theory for IM3: 3 dB/dB; field values typically 2.2-2.8 dB/dB.
The PIM the analyzer, test lead and adapters make themselves, measured into a low-PIM load.
A 50-ohm load built to generate very little PIM; the reference for residual checks and for terminating ports.
A device that produces a known IM3 level at a stated power and frequency, used to check the analyzer reads correctly.
PIM measured without movement or stress.
PIM measured while tapping connectors/devices and flexing cables to reveal loose or unstable joints.
Fixed F1/F2, IM level plotted over time; used for static and tap tests.
One tone fixed, the other swept, so the IM product moves across the receive band; avoids false passes from phase cancellation.
PIM measured travelling back toward the source port - what field analyzers measure.
PIM measured at the output of a two-port device.
1-port: both tones out one port. 2-port: F1 and F2 out separate ports/antennas so they mix only beyond the antennas (external cross-band PIM).
IM magnitude vs distance along the line and beyond the antenna (Anritsu term).
Kaelus term for distance to PIM and return-loss faults.
Return loss or VSWR vs distance from a swept measurement; maps connectors and damage.
Cable velocity factor used to convert time/frequency data to distance; use 1.0 for distances in air.
A strong PIM source (bagged steel wool) taped to the radome to show the antenna's position on a DTP trace.
Internal: inside the feed/antenna. External: from objects in front of or near the antenna, or where two antennas' signals mix.
PIM from corroded metal (fences, roofs, mast bolts, AC ducts) excited by nearby transmit signals.
Breakdown of thin oxide films between contacts; produces bursty wideband interference.
Iron, nickel, cobalt and some alloys; strong PIM generators - avoid in RF current paths (incl. nickel plating, stainless steel).
Impedance-match measures from a line sweep; independent of PIM - a line can pass one and fail the other.
Uneven uplink noise between the two receive paths of a sector; a classic sign of PIM in the noisy path.
Distributed antenna system: passive (coax, splitters, couplers) or active/hybrid (fiber to remote units) network distributing RF indoors.
A DAS owner/operator that carries several carriers on one shared system.
Head-end point where operators' signals are combined and fed into the DAS; MCF tests PIM at each input.
Unequal power divider (e.g., 6 dB coupled / 1.7 dB through) that taps signal off a riser to a floor.
Equal-split combiner (3 dB per stage) used to combine radios; unused ports need loads.
Emergency responder communication enhancement system - in-building public safety radio coverage (IFC 510, NFPA 1225).
Signal booster used in ERCES and some DAS; an active device - do not inject PIM test tones into it.
Delivered Audio Quality 3.0 - the ERCES coverage benchmark (speech understandable with repetition only rarely required).
IEC series on measuring PIM in passive RF devices: Part 1 general, 2 cable assemblies, 3 connectors, 4 cables, 5 filters, 6 antennas, 7 field measurements, 8 radiated PIM of objects.
Detecting PIM from the baseband side using the site's own radios and live or test signals, without disconnecting coax.

pim_sources.why: Gaps and low contact pressure make non-linear junctions; the most common field fault (e.g., a loose back nut on a jumper).
pim_sources.fix: Torque to the manufacturer's value with a calibrated wrench; tap test.

pim_sources.why: Over-tightening distorts contact surfaces and damages the centre conductor; first instinct to over-tighten usually makes it worse.
pim_sources.fix: Replace damaged parts; use the correct torque, not more.

pim_sources.source: Dirt, metal flakes, debris in connectors
pim_sources.why: Particles from cutting and repeated mating touch current-carrying surfaces; intermittent PIM as cables flex.
pim_sources.fix: Cut with the cable facing down, deburr, blow out, alcohol-clean, inspect.

pim_sources.source: Foam dielectric or adhesive trapped in the joint
pim_sources.why: Blocks metal-to-metal contact (DAS field case near two antennas).
pim_sources.fix: Re-work the connector; remove foam and glue.

pim_sources.why: Oxide films act like diodes; worst in coastal humidity and salt air.
pim_sources.fix: Clean regularly in coastal areas; weatherproof; replace corroded parts.

pim_sources.why: Iron/nickel/cobalt are strong PIM sources: stainless steel can add 10-20 dB, nickel or gold-over-nickel plating 20-40 dB.
pim_sources.fix: Use non-ferrous connectors plated with silver, white bronze or gold; avoid nickel and non-magnetic stainless in current paths.

pim_sources.why: Ferrite devices can be prominent IM sources.
pim_sources.fix: Minimize them in high-power paths; PIM-test them.

pim_sources.why: Galvanic corrosion risk.
pim_sources.fix: Avoid dissimilar-metal junctions.

pim_sources.why: The braid acts like hundreds of loose connections, worse with age (LMR400, RG214 named).
pim_sources.fix: Use solid-outer-conductor cable; braided only where the carrier approves single-band use.

pim_sources.why: Seams in shielding corrode; plated copper can flake off aluminium cores; water in the line.
pim_sources.fix: Replace; use quality cable; keep water out.

pim_sources.why: Sun warms cables, changing electrical length and contact state; PIM can appear hot and vanish cold or vice versa.
pim_sources.fix: Repeat tests at different times; repair marginal joints.

pim_sources.why: Fatigue breaks, cold solder joints, corrosion; weak connector mounts loosen after a few torque cycles; most pre-2006 antennas were not built for PIM.
pim_sources.fix: Ground-test antennas on non-metal stands facing clear sky; keep a known-good antenna; limit torque cycles.

pim_sources.why: Corroded fences, roofs, mast bolts, AC ducts, guard rails, billboards, roofing materials near antennas.
pim_sources.fix: Locate with DTP + PIM marker and probe; remove/replace/insulate the object or move the antenna; document for the owner.

pim_sources.why: Small DAS antennas excite nearby metal - cable trays, vent pipes, AC units, flashing, loose hardware - often behind the antenna.
pim_sources.fix: Keep 500 mm clear; relocate within about 1 m; avoid concealed/low-profile antennas without a backplane.

pim_sources.why: As they age their breakdown voltage drops until RF peaks cause micro-arcing.
pim_sources.fix: Test and replace aged arrestors.

pim_sources.why: Often high IM3; harmful where several operators/bands share the hybrid.
pim_sources.fix: Use low-PIM cable loads at multi-operator points.

pim_sources.why: Thinner coatings and more ferromagnetic content; degrade faster with corrosion and handling.
pim_sources.fix: Buy from approved material lists with published PIM specs and factory test data.

pim_sources.why: Installers not trained in carrier-grade RF termination; problems surface only at PIM test.
pim_sources.fix: Manufacturer training; correct prep tools; factory-made jumpers.

pim_sources.why: Components hanging on cables or weak anchors stress connectors; PIM becomes erratic.
pim_sources.fix: Mount solidly, add strain relief, leave wrench access.

pim_sources.why: Seals on test cables collect metal shavings; precision line-sweep adapters are not low-PIM; tools and safety belts near antennas create PIM.
pim_sources.fix: No seals on test cables; low-PIM adapters only; residual check; clear the antenna field.

pim_sources.source: N-type connectors in high-power multi-carrier paths
pim_sources.why: Very small male outer-conductor contact area, easily damaged by over-torque; sensitive to torque and vibration.
pim_sources.fix: Prefer 4.3-10 or 7-16 where possible; torque N carefully.
